Let \( A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots \) be a sequence of finite nonempty sets of positive integers. Given that \( |A_i \cap A_j| = \gcd(i, j) \) for all (not necessarily distinct) positive integers \( i \) and \( j \), compute the minimum possible value of

\[
\sum_{d|250} \max A_d,
\]

where the sum ranges over all positive integer divisors \( d \) of 250.

(For a finite nonempty set \( S \), we define \( \max S \) as the largest element of \( S \).)


Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
\[
\boxed{499}
\]

Here is the reasoning.

First note that taking \(i=j\) gives

\[
|A_i|=\gcd(i,i)=i.
\]

If \(a\mid b\), then

\[
|A_a\cap A_b|=\gcd(a,b)=a=|A_a|,
\]

so \(A_a\subseteq A_b\). Therefore, for all \(i,j\),

\[
A_i\cap A_j=A_{\gcd(i,j)}.
\]

Now consider any positive integer \(x\) that appears in some \(A_i\). Let

\[
S_x=\{i: x\in A_i\}.
\]

From the above, \(S_x\) is upward-closed under divisibility and closed under gcd:

- if \(i\in S_x\) and \(i\mid j\), then \(j\in S_x\);
- if \(i,j\in S_x\), then \(\gcd(i,j)\in S_x\).

One can show that \(S_x\) must be exactly the set of multiples of a unique positive integer \(m\). Call this \(m\) the type of \(x\). Thus \(x\in A_i\) if and only if \(m\mid i\).

Let \(c_m\) be the number of elements of type \(m\). Then for every \(i\),

\[
|A_i|=\sum_{m\mid i} c_m=i.
\]

The unique nonnegative integer solution to this divisor-sum equation is

\[
c_m=\varphi(m),
\]

because \(\sum_{m\mid i}\varphi(m)=i\). Hence, for every divisor \(d\mid 250\), there are exactly \(\varphi(d)\) elements whose type is \(d\), and all of these elements lie in \(A_d\).

Let \(T_d\) be the set of elements of type \(d\), for \(d\mid 250\). The sets \(T_d\) are pairwise disjoint and

\[
|T_d|=\varphi(d).
\]

Since \(T_d\subseteq A_d\),

\[
\max A_d\ge \max T_d.
\]

So it remains to minimize the sum of the maxima of eight disjoint finite sets of positive integers with sizes

\[
\varphi(1),\varphi(2),\varphi(5),\varphi(10),\varphi(25),\varphi(50),\varphi(125),\varphi(250).
\]

These sizes are

\[
1,1,4,4,20,20,100,100.
\]

For disjoint sets of sizes \(a_1,\dots,a_8\), the minimum possible sum of their maxima is obtained by taking the union to be \(\{1,2,\dots,\sum a_i\}\) and arranging the sets as initial intervals in nondecreasing order of size. The corresponding maxima are the cumulative sums:

\[
1,\;2,\;6,\;10,\;30,\;50,\;150,\;250.
\]

Their sum is

\[
1+2+6+10+30+50+150+250=499.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{d\mid 250}\max A_d\ge 499.
\]

It remains to show this bound is attainable. For each \(m\), take \(\varphi(m)\) distinct labels of type \(m\). For the divisors of \(250\), assign labels as follows:

\[
\begin{aligned}
T_1&=\{1\},\\
T_2&=\{2\},\\
T_5&=\{3,4,5,6\},\\
T_{10}&=\{7,8,9,10\},\\
T_{25}&=\{11,\dots,30\},\\
T_{50}&=\{31,\dots,50\},\\
T_{125}&=\{51,\dots,150\},\\
T_{250}&=\{151,\dots,250\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For all other types \(m\nmid 250\), assign distinct labels larger than \(250\). Define

\[
A_i=\bigcup_{m\mid i} T_m.
\]

Then

\[
|A_i|=\sum_{m\mid i}\varphi(m)=i
\]

and

\[
|A_i\cap A_j|=\sum_{m\mid \gcd(i,j)}\varphi(m)=\gcd(i,j).
\]

For the divisors of \(250\), the chosen order

\[
1,2,5,10,25,50,125,250
\]

respects divisibility, so for each \(d\mid 250\), the largest maximum among the \(T_m\) with \(m\mid d\) is exactly \(\max T_d\). Therefore the relevant maxima are

\[
1,2,6,10,30,50,150,250,
\]

whose sum is \(499\).

Hence the minimum possible value is

\[
\boxed{499}.
\]
